name: United Monarchy (Saul, David, Solomon)

objectives.text: Identify Saul, David, and Solomon as the first three kings of Israel
Retell the story of David and Goliath, naming David's trust in the Lord as the reason he faced the giant
Describe how David and Jonathan showed loyal friendship to each other
Name Solomon as the king who built the Temple as God's house in Jerusalem
Retell how Solomon asked God for wisdom instead of riches or long life
Recall that David wrote songs to God found in the book of Psalms and recite Psalm 23
Summarize how God chose David by looking at his heart rather than his outward appearance
Explain why Israel asked Samuel for a king and why the request displeased Samuel and the Lord
Describe how David refused to harm Saul because Saul was the Lord's anointed
Explain why Saul lost the kingdom by citing his disobedience to God's commands
Describe David's kindness to Mephibosheth as keeping his promise to Jonathan
Sequence the major events of the reigns of Saul, David, and Solomon on a timeline
Compare David's confession of sin after Nathan's rebuke with Saul's excuses after his disobedience
Identify the wisdom writings the Bible associates with Solomon
Analyze how Solomon's many wives, horses, and wealth broke the law for Israel's kings and led him away from the Lord
Analyze the promises God made to David in the Davidic Covenant and their place in the covenant of grace
Explain the purpose of the Temple as the place of God's presence among his people and of prayer to him
Interpret the political and spiritual significance of David making Jerusalem his capital and bringing the ark there
Connect Solomon's Temple dedication prayer to God's purpose of making his name known among the nations
Trace the consequences of David's sin with Bathsheba through the later troubles in his family
Analyze how the narrator of Samuel shows the Lord establishing David's rise despite Saul's opposition
Explain how God kept his covenant promise to David even while judging Solomon's unfaithfulness
Evaluate the role of the prophets Samuel, Nathan, and Gad in holding Israel's kings accountable to God's word
Construct a profile of the promised Messianic King from the Davidic promises and their New Testament fulfillment in Christ
Evaluate the tension between God's kingship over Israel and the establishment of a human monarchy
Analyze the wealth and trade of Solomon's kingdom using the biblical record alongside historical and archaeological sources
Compare the portrayal of David and Solomon in Chronicles with their portrayal in Samuel and Kings and explain the purpose of each account
Develop a written argument showing how the kingdom, Temple, and wisdom of the United Monarchy point forward to their fulfillment in Christ

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (kings identified, David and Goliath, Temple builder, Psalms, heart over appearance, Saul's loss, David versus Saul repentance, Davidic Covenant, Jerusalem, dedication prayer, Bathsheba consequences, Messianic King profile, theocracy tension, Solomon's wealth now framed as source analysis, typology now a fulfillment argument). Replaced the vague 'apply lessons' objective with an analysis of Solomon's fall against Deuteronomy 17. Added missing content: Israel's request for a king, David and Jonathan, Solomon's request for wisdom, David sparing Saul, Mephibosheth, timeline sequencing, Solomon's wisdom writings, Temple purpose, the narrator's portrayal of God's sovereignty, covenant faithfulness amid judgment, prophetic accountability, and Chronicles versus Samuel-Kings. Anchored each objective with verse-level references and replaced loose confession citations with precise ones (WCF 7.3, 8.1, 15.2, WSC Q26, Q87, Heidelberg Q31).
